name: Steps for Installing a Weather-Tight Basement Entry Door

step.name: Step 1: Inspect the foundation wall and exterior drainage
step.text: Check the existing concrete or masonry opening for cracks, structural settling, and signs of active seepage. Measure the exterior ground slope to verify that surrounding soil and downspouts route runoff away from the entry pit before starting any framing work.

step.name: Step 2: Confirm structural framing and rough opening dimensions
step.text: Verify whether the foundation opening is load-bearing and calculate the necessary header support. Measure height, width, and squareness, clearing away broken mortar, loose concrete, and deteriorating lumber so new framing anchors securely into solid masonry.

step.name: Step 3: Fit the sill pan and apply primary water flashing
step.text: Clean the concrete footing thoroughly and set a durable, continuous sill pan along the bottom edge. Layer waterproof flashing tape along the rough opening sides and integrate head flashing at the top to direct water away from the wall core.

step.name: Step 4: Anchor the door unit and level the jambs
step.text: Set the pre-hung exterior door assembly into the prepared opening over beds of high-grade sealant. Use non-corrosive masonry fasteners and shims to ensure the side jambs are plumb, the head jamb is level, and the unit operates smoothly without binding.

step.name: Step 5: Insulate perimeter cavities and adjust the threshold
step.text: Fill the gaps between the rough opening and door jamb with low-expansion foam insulation to stop thermal drafts. Adjust the threshold height to create a snug seal against the bottom weatherstrip, making sure exterior water sheds directly outward.

step.name: Step 6: Install hardware, exterior trim, and final sealants
step.text: Fasten exterior casing, deadbolts, and latch sets, then tool exterior-grade sealant around all exterior joints. Test latching and confirm that weatherstripping makes uniform contact around the entire perimeter.
